mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot e-2008 electric motor replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Peugeot e-2008 electric motor typically costs £1,200-£2,500 for a used unit, £2,000-£3,800 for a reconditioned unit, or £2,500-£4,500 for a rebuilt unit with 12-month warranty. Supply & fit labour adds approximately £600-£1,000 due to EV-specific procedures.

mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot e-2008 battery replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Peugeot e-2008 traction battery replacement typically costs £3,000-£5,000 for a used unit, £4,500-£7,000 for a reconditioned unit, or £8,000-£12,000 for a new OEM battery. The battery is covered by an 8-year / 100,000-mile warranty (70% capacity retained).

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of on-board charger failure in a Peugeot e-2008?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common sign is the car refusing to charge on AC (Type 2) while still charging on DC rapid chargers. Other symptoms include intermittent charging, "charge interrupted" errors, and no diagnostic warning lights on the dashboard.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the battery or motor in a Peugeot e-2008?

acceptedAnswer.text: For an e-2008 worth £12,000-£22,000, replacement is often worthwhile if the rest of the car is in good condition. If battery health is below 70% and the vehicle is under 8 years / 100,000 miles, the battery may be covered under warranty.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot e-2008 electric motor or battery replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most Peugeot e-2008 components are dispatched within 48-72 hours, with supply & fit installation typically completed within 2-3 working days at approved EV specialists due to high-voltage safety procedures.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with Peugeot e-2008 replacement motors and batteries?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rebuilt Peugeot e-2008 electric motors include a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Reconditioned batteries typically include 12-month cover. Used components carry 3-6 months cover depending on supplier terms.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 50kWh and 54kWh e-2008 batteries?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 50kWh battery was introduced at launch (2019) with the 100kW (136hp) motor, offering up to 206 miles WLTP range. The 54kWh battery arrived in 2021 with the 115kW (156hp) motor, offering up to 247 miles WLTP range. In 2024, the 50kWh option was reintroduced as a lower-cost entry point.

historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot e-2008 - Electric Powertrain History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Peugeot e-2008 arrived in 2019 as the all-electric variant of the second-generation 2008, sharing the CMP platform with the e-208. It combines a front-mounted electric motor with a lithium-ion battery pack, offering zero-emission driving with competitive range for urban and suburban use.

milestones.description: e-2008 launched with 100kW (136hp) electric motor and 50kWh battery, WLTP range up to 206 miles
54kWh battery option introduced with 115kW (156hp/154bhp) motor, WLTP range up to 247 miles
On-board charger (OBC) issues identified on models produced up to November 2022
100kW (136hp) motor with 50kWh battery re-introduced as lower-cost entry option

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot e-2008 Electric Powertrain Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot e-2008 is generally a reliable electric vehicle - it scored 92.0% in the 2025 What Car? Reliability Survey - but on-board charger failures, battery degradation and Battery Monitoring Unit faults dominate replacement enquiries. Every rebuilt electric motor or reconditioned battery supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Use the problem groups below to compare repair costs versus replacement value for your specific e-2008.

problems.h4: On-Board Charger Failure - Why e-2008 Models Won't Charge on AC
problems.rootCause: The 11kW on-board charger (OBC) - which converts AC mains power to DC for the battery - can fail, preventing AC charging via Type 2 cables. DC rapid charging (CCS) may still function.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; may not resolve hardware faults

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove faulty OBC; fit new/reconditioned unit; recalibrate system
repairOptions.longevity: Addresses root cause; may require battery disconnect and HV safety procedures

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt Drive Unit with New OBC
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt motor with new OBC and updated software, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best value when motor shows additional wear or vehicle has 60k+ miles

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Peugeot e-2008 of 2020-2022 vintage is worth approximately £12,000-£22,000 depending on mileage and battery health. For vehicles worth over £15,000, OBC replacement is cost-effective. For vehicles approaching £12,000, evaluate whether a used drive unit offers better value.
problems.recommendation: If your e-2008 won't charge on AC but works on DC rapid chargers, the OBC is the likely culprit. Stellantis has acknowledged this issue and may cover repairs on models produced up to November 2022 - check with your local Peugeot dealer first. If out of warranty, a specialist OBC replacement is significantly cheaper than dealer pricing.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt ZK01 Peugeot e-2008 electric motor prices

problems.h4: Battery Degradation & BMU Faults - Why e-2008 Range Drops Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Lithium-ion batteries naturally degrade over time, but some e-2008 owners report over 20% capacity loss within two years - significantly higher than the expected 2.5% per year. Battery Monitoring Unit (BMU) software faults can also cause inaccurate readings and sudden power loss.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnostic recalibration; BMU software update; battery health check
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caused by software glitch; may not resolve hardware faults

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - Battery Cell Balancing / Module Replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Identify weak cells; replace individual modules; recalibrate BMS
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective if only one or two modules are degraded

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit reconditioned battery with cells matched and balanced, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best value when battery health is below 70% or multiple modules are failing

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a Peugeot e-2008, the traction battery is the most valuable component. If battery health drops below 70% (the warranty threshold), replacement may be covered under the 8-year / 100,000-mile warranty. If out of warranty, a reconditioned battery is significantly cheaper than a new OEM unit - but ensure the cost doesn't exceed the vehicle's value.
problems.recommendation: Have your e-2008's battery health checked annually using a specialist EV diagnostic tool. If range has dropped noticeably, a BMU reset or cell balancing may restore some capacity. If battery health is below 70% and the vehicle is under 8 years / 100,000 miles, contact your Peugeot dealer for warranty claim. For out-of-warranty vehicles, a reconditioned battery from a specialist offers the best value.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for Peugeot e-2008 traction battery replacement

problems.h4: Sudden Power Loss - Why e-2008 Models Enter Limp Mode
problems.rootCause: A recall affecting approximately 1,100 e-2008 vehicles relates to an over-sensitive 'open circuit detection system' that can cause sudden power loss. Battery Monitoring Unit (BMU) faults can also cause invalid cell voltage readings leading to stalling.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Dealer recall work; BMU software update; system reset
repairOptions.longevity: Free if vehicle is affected by the recall; check with your dealer

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace faulty BMU or ECU module; recalibrate system
repairOptions.longevity: Addresses root cause if software update doesn't resolve

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt Drive Unit with Updated Electronics
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt motor with updated BMU/ECU, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best value when power loss has caused secondary damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For any Peugeot e-2008, check if your vehicle is affected by the open circuit detection system recall - repairs are free. If out of recall scope, a specialist diagnosis is significantly cheaper than dealer rates.
problems.recommendation: If your e-2008 experiences sudden power loss or stalling, contact your local Peugeot dealer immediately to check if your vehicle is affected by the recall. If not, have the BMU and ECU diagnosed by a specialist EV technician - early intervention prevents more serious component damage.
